deviations:
V1 #2, the PrecisionTrace header: the ruling's figures were not taken; the rest of the item was applied. I measured both, and both are false:
- 'up to about 3x that attempt': x3.4 is the whole hand-off's ratio to round 1's. The tree against the single attempt it replaces is up to x46 on V1's own chains and x97 on a peeling chain, because that attempt can stop after one scan.
- 'under 0.5 ms on 256 points': a 256-point peeling chain that one attempt settles costs 0.514-0.518 ms in the tree.
The header now says: the tree keeps the same points at a fraction of the cost of several attempts. Where one attempt suffices, the whole tree can cost far more than that attempt, which may stop at its first segment: up to about 0.5 ms on 256 points, where every split sheds one point (M4's fix round 3). The peel is the tree's structural worst case: (n−1)(n−2)/2 distances.

rules_meta.diff design: only a call in parentheses can be the emptiness test, so next{} == nil is now flagged. This is a constant test, and the lead's rule already meant 'one argument'. In the patch, the comments above BANNED_GLOBALS and nextCalls serve as 'its header'. The long `if` is wrapped in the file's own style.

Rewrapping: rewrapped paragraphs never break inside inline code. Without this, slice 10's command would split over two lines. In the Source.spec header, the new examples are set in backticks so they do not split. The E-S3.10 and notes hunks are line-identical to V1's tried diff; the cell and slice 10 use V2's exact words.
